statusText: Roughly five hours into the U.S. cash session, the Nasdaq-100 complex remains firm as the S&P 500 holds its record push above 7,800, with leadership broadening into semiconductors (Sandisk reported up ~15%, Micron ~5.6%) and the Nasdaq Composite up roughly 0.9-1.2% on the day. A flat July PPI print continues to reinforce Wednesday's benign CPI and lower Fed-hike odds, while WTI crude fell about 1.4% to roughly $81-82. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily budget is fully exhausted this run (TREASURY_YIELD rejected immediately with a rate_limit error), so this assessment leans on web reporting alone; QQQ intraday quotes and NQ futures levels returned by search are identical to the prior six consecutive hourly checks and are treated as stale rather than confirming fresh structure. No failed-pullback or repeated-extension price action has been identified, so Tail stays low. Stress holds in the moderate band, ticking up modestly as the session approaches its 20:00 UTC close and tonight's Applied Materials earnings call (~20:30 UTC), with the unresolved Iran/Hormuz standoff -- Iran's Basij commander again asserting the strait is 'under Iran's control' against U.S. claims of transit access, no new kinetic escalation -- as a secondary, unchanged overhang.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Reassess around the 20:00 UTC cash close and Applied Materials' after-close earnings call (~20:30 UTC), and again ahead of tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print and 14:00 UTC UMich sentiment release; an upgrade to a higher Tail state requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks, not the pending catalysts or today's data-feed limitations themselves.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its record-high push -- S&P 500 above 7,800 with broadening semiconductor leadership -- as oil slides and Alpha Vantage's daily budget runs out; Tail stays low while Stress ticks up modestly into tonight's cash close and Applied Materials earnings
body: Roughly five hours after the 13:30 UTC cash open, web reporting confirms the Nasdaq-100 complex continues to hold its advance: the S&P 500 sits at a fresh record above 7,800, and the Nasdaq Composite is reported up roughly 0.9-1.2% on the day with leadership broadening into semiconductors -- Sandisk reported up about 15% and Micron about 5.6% -- alongside continued strength in Microsoft, Nvidia and Apple. QQQ and NQ futures quotes returned by web search this run are numerically identical to the figures returned in each of the prior six consecutive hourly checks (QQQ ~730.28/+1.05%, NQ ~29,805.75 last), which is treated as a stale, cached read rather than confirmation of unchanged live structure; neither is used to assert fresh intraday price-path detail this run, and the broader index-level reporting (S&P record, Composite %, sector leadership) is used as the primary corroborating evidence instead. A flat July producer price index continues to reinforce Wednesday's benign CPI print and reduced Fed-hike odds. WTI crude fell about 1.4% to roughly $81-82/bbl, continuing its recent slide. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily request budget is fully exhausted this run: the first call (TREASURY_YIELD, 2-year) returned an explicit rate_limit error citing the 25-request/day cap, so no further Alpha Vantage calls were attempted to avoid wasting budget; both the 2Y/10Y Treasury yield and QQQ GLOBAL_QUOTE therefore remain unconfirmed beyond Wednesday's close levels (10Y ~4.68%) carried forward from prior runs. VIX likewise has no fresh Thursday print available via search and is carried forward near Wednesday's close (~14.4, a seven-month low), consistent with continued volatility compression but not independently confirmed intraday. Applied Materials still reports fiscal Q3 earnings after today's close, with its call at 20:30 UTC (4:30pm ET); consensus expects roughly $9.0B revenue and $3.38 non-GAAP EPS, in line with management's own guidance range, with the stock trading well below its 2026 high into the print. Iran's Hormuz standoff remains unresolved and unchanged in substance since the prior run: Iran's Basij commander again asserted the strait is 'under Iran's control' while Iranian officials dispute U.S. claims of unimpeded transit access; no new kinetic escalation or market-transmission event has been identified. Given the continued advance with no observed failed-retracement or repeated-extension structure, and the absence of any new escalatory or macro shock, Tail holds at 16%, still low. Stress ticks up modestly to 38% (from 32%) as the session moves toward its 20:00 UTC close and tonight's AMAT earnings call, and as this run's confirming data is thinner than the prior run's (zero successful Alpha Vantage calls versus two last run); it stays within the moderate band, below the elevated threshold, since no new shock has actually printed. Confidence eases to 48% (from 54%), reflecting the complete Alpha Vantage rate-limit this run, Treasury/VIX levels now carried forward from Wednesday's close, and QQQ/NQ search quotes confirmed stale across six consecutive hourly checks, partially offset by fresh, quantified web corroboration of the oil decline and semiconductor-led breadth.

forecastDetail.comment: Roughly five hours into the cash session, price action continues to track today's advance with no observed failed-pullback structure; Alpha Vantage's Treasury/quote feeds were rate-limited this run and NQ futures remain a stale cached read, so today's incremental confirmation leans on S&P/Composite-level reporting and a falling WTI print.

Stress builds toward the mid-40s as the session moves into its final hour before the 20:00 UTC cash close and tonight's Applied Materials earnings call; Tail stays low absent any observed one-way extension.

The 20:00 UTC cash close coincides with Applied Materials' 20:30 UTC earnings call; Stress peaks for the day on event/whipsaw risk from a semiconductor-equipment earnings reaction, though pre-event alignment is not treated as already observed.
The AMAT after-hours reaction continues to resolve into the evening; Stress stays elevated within the moderate band until the initial post-earnings move is confirmed one way or the other.
As the post-earnings reaction settles and Asian trading has not yet opened, Stress eases back toward the day's lower range with no confirmed failed-retracement structure carried into the close.
Late-evening liquidity thins further with no confirmed AMAT-driven follow-through; Stress continues easing toward the overnight low absent new catalysts.
